title: Variant prioritization ladder and control-plane notes
content:
Purpose and context:
This note enumerates a lightweight, operationally-sane approach to keep latency-sensitive inference online during capacity pressure by using a "priority ladder" for model variants, probabilistic downgrade, and a small control-plane DSL for cross-region spillover. Goal: minimize user-visible errors and latency spikes while preserving a predictable unit-cost profile.

Key ideas (short):
- Priority ladder: ordered list of model variants (high-fidelity -> medium -> fast-quant -> smallest). Each variant has a capacity weight and a fidelity score.
- Fractional routing: rather than all-or-nothing fallback, route a configurable fraction of traffic to lower tiers to test quality and reduce pressure.
- Region-aware warm pools: maintain small warm pools of cheaper variants in DR regions for fast spillover.
- Control plane DSL: express routing rules and budget windows (token budgets, per-minute qps cap, fidelity floor).

Operational primitives:
1) Variant descriptor (example fields):
   - variant_id: string
   - family: gpt-3-like / llama2 / open-weights
   - fidelity_score: 0.0-1.0
   - latency_p50, latency_p95 (ms)
   - cost_per_token_usd (estimated)
   - capacity_weight: integer (used in weighted allocation)
   - compatible_fallbacks: list of variant_ids (ordered)

2) Control rule (pseudo-DSL):
   WHEN region.qps > region.capacity_threshold AND region.slo.latency_p95 > Xms
   SET routing_fraction(target_variant: "fast-quant", fraction: 0.25, for: 5m)
   TAG tenants where priority >= gold FOR fraction_exemptions

3) Hedging/cascade policy:
   - Soft degrade: probabilistic downgrade where N% of requests are sent to cheaper variant but majority still try primary with fast early-exit if token budget reached.
   - Hard degrade: circuit-break primary for region and route 100% to next variant family.

Multi-region spillover pattern (novel twist: skew-aware spillover):
- Track skew: measurement of how imbalanced regional load is relative to capacity (skew = qps / capacity).
- If skew > 1.2 in region A, compute candidate spillover to region B using penalty function that favors regions with spare capacity and low network RTT for the tenant.
- Apply gradual traffic shift: 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 3 windows (2m each) with quality checks at each step (LLM outputs sampled against golden prompts).
- If quality drift > threshold, abort and backoff to previous step.

Per-tenant degradation profile:
- Tenants can define an SLO importance. For example: {gold: no degrade under 99pct of normal qps, silver: allow soft degrade after 90pct, bronze: aggressive degrade at 70pct}.
- Profiles map to exception lists in the control plane DSL.

Token-budget enforcement and early exit:
- Add per-request token budget and fast-path early-exit in runtime: if aggregated token burn in a window would push region over budget, send an early STOP to in-flight low-priority requests (graceful truncation) and mark as degraded.
- Emit explicit telemetry: degrade_reason=token_budget_exceeded and report sample of output for quality monitoring.

Quality validation and guardrails:
- Canary sampling: always mirror 1% of degraded traffic to the primary model (shadow) for offline Q checks.
- Prompt-set probes: 20 curated prompts, run every 30s on candidate variant during ramp to detect semantic regressions.
- Acceptance thresholds: embedding-similarity >= 0.92 and token-overlap heuristics. These are mutable knobs.

Telemetry and alerting (novel metrics):
- regional_skew (float), variant_fallback_rate (by tenant), degrade_burst_index (counts of sudden hard-degrades), shadow_similarity_drop (percent decrease in daily probe similarity).
- Alerts: degrade_burst_index > 5 in 1m -> paged; shadow_similarity_drop > 0.05 over 10m -> ticket to ML team.

Control plane design notes:
- Keep rules small and composable. Each rule should declare scope (global/region/tenant), trigger (simple predicates on existing metrics), and action (route_fraction / set_capacity_weight / open_circuit).
- Conflict resolution: rules have priority integer. For overlapping rules, higher priority wins; lower-priority rules may be sampled for experiments only.
- Fast-path control: an RPC cache in edge proxies that refreshes rule deltas every 2s (delta only). Full rule recompute on leader change.

Example workload scenarios (walkthroughs):
1) Sudden spike in EMEA region (x1.8 normal)
   - Step 0: region enters pressure window. Run rule: enable soft degrade for bronze tenants, route 15% -> fast-quant.
   - Step 1 (2m): probe similarity unchanged -> increase to 40% and add warm-pool instances in neighboring EU region.
   - Step 2: if latency still > p95 target or cost overruns, escalate to hard degrade for bronze only and stop auto-scale beyond reserved capacity for host model.

2) Long tail outage (zone down in us-west)
   - Circuit-break zone; immediate increase of regional spillover score and trigger cross-region fanout for gold tenants (synchronous), silver asynchronous with retry budget, bronze best-effort.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How aggressive should fractional routing be before we do full circuit-break? (suggest experiment matrix: 10/30/60% ramps)
- Quality checks: embedding-similarity threshold is brittle across model families. Consider hybrid checks (BLEU-like + task-specific eval).
- Do we allow per-request overrides (client asks for degrade:false) and how to enforce fairness? (risk: tenants can opt-out and starve the pool)
- Cost accounting: metric granularity for billing when a request is partially served by two variants (hedged requests).

Action items and TODOs:
- [ ] Implement minimal Rule DSL parser in control plane (PR drafted: runtime/pull/214).
- [ ] Add regional_skew and variant_fallback_rate to telemetry pipeline (SLO: ship by 2024-11-15).
- [ ] Design experiment: 3-week A/B across silver tenants with fractional routing strategies (owners: Priya/Mateo).
- [ ] Create runbook snippets for SRE on hard degrade rollback steps.

Notes to self / freeform thoughts:
- Keep default ladder conservative: prefer shortfall mitigation via batching and KV caching before degrading quality.
- Warm pools could be cheaper variants pre-warmed with KV caches to reduce cold-start delta when spilling over.
- Consider a "degradation score" per tenant that decays over 24h to avoid oscillation.

References / links:
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/214
- Jira: JIRA-PLAT-8721 (control plane rule DSL)
- Slack thread: #infra-fallback (arch brainstorm 2024-10-10)

If this reads OK, I'll turn this into a short RFC and include a simple state-machine diagram for the rule transitions.

-- jordan
